   224	  rule roundFN(F:Float, N:Int)
   225	    => Int2Float(roundF(F *Float Int2Float(10 ^Int N, 53, 11)), 53, 11)
   226	       /Float Int2Float(10 ^Int N, 53, 11) [concrete]
   227	  rule applyBuiltin("round", F:Float, .Vals)        => roundF(F)
   228	  rule applyBuiltin("round", F:Float, N:Int, .Vals) => roundFN(F, N)
   229	
   230	  syntax Float ::= sqrtF(Float) [function, total, symbol(sqrtF), no-evaluators]
   231	  rule sqrtF(F:Float) => sqrtFloat(F) [concrete]
   232	  syntax KItem ::= "#mathSqrt"
   233	  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "sqrt"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathSqrt ... </k> [priority(40)]
   234	  rule <k> F:Float ~> #mathSqrt => sqrtF(F) ... </k>
   235	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #mathSqrt => sqrtF(intToF(I)) ... </k>
   236	
   237	  // ---- min / max over a FLOAT list — FLOAT branch of the shared #minCont0/#maxCont0 folds (which
   238	  // seed/step with `requires isInt(V)`, so they are STUCK on floats). These add the `requires
   239	  // isFloat(V)` seed + a Float-accumulator fold via K's minFloat/maxFloat — concrete for krun. A proof
   240	  // over a SYMBOLIC float list intercepts min/max problem-locally to an opaque minVF/maxVF (at
   241	  // #applyK, priority 40, in its verification.k) BEFORE #minAcc0, so this fold is krun-only. Additive:
   242	  // the isFloat guard is disjoint from the existing isInt one.
   243	  syntax KItem ::= #maxAccF(Iterable, Float) | #maxContF(Float)
   244	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
   245	  rule <k> #maxAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxContF(M) ... </k>
   246	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
   247	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => #maxAccF(R, maxFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   248	       requires isFloat(V)
   249	
   250	  syntax KItem ::= #minAccF(Iterable, Float) | #minContF(Float)
   251	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
   252	  rule <k> #minAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minContF(M) ... </k>
   253	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
   254	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minContF(M:Float) => #minAccF(R, minFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   255	       requires isFloat(V)
   256	
   257	  // ---- sum over a float list (krun; mirrors the min/max float paths). The Int-only shared
   258	  // #sumCont sticks on a Float yield; switch to a Float-headed fold via addF (concrete twin).
   259	  // The switch guard carries the SYNTACTIC negation of the Int rule's guard so a symbolic proof
   260	  // with isInt(V) in its path condition refutes this branch without sort reasoning.
   261	  syntax KItem ::= #sumAccF(Iterable, Float) | #sumContF(Float)
   262	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
   263	        => #sumAccF(R, addF(intToF(ACC), {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   264	       requires isFloat(V) andBool notBool (isInt(V) orBool isBool(V))
   265	  rule <k> #sumAccF(IT:Iterable, ACC:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumContF(ACC) ... </k>
   266	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float) => ACC ... </k>
   267	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
   268	        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
   269	       requires isFloat(V)
   270	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
   271	        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, intToF(intOf(V)))) ... </k>
   272	       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)
   273	endmodule
FILE semantics/operators.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule
FILE semantics/functions.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/functions.k — MPY-FUNCTIONS
     2	
     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
FILE semantics/call.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    75	
    76	  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
    78	  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
    79	  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
    80	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    81	        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    82	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    83	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
    84	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    85	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    86	
    87	  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
    88	  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
    90	       <env> L:Int </env>
    91	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
    93	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
    94	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
    95	endmodule

     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>

    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]

    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)

    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on

    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]

    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B

    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule
FILE semantics/list.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/tuple.k — MPY-TUPLE
     2	
     3	module MPY-TUPLE
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-LIST
     7	  imports MPY-METHODS
     8	
     9	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's tuple case) ======================
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    11	  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, tuple(R)) ... </k>
    12	
    13	  // ==== TupleExpr: tuple(ValSeq) literal + == != ===========================
    14	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toTuple"
    15	  rule <k> TupleExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toTuple) ... </k>
    16	  rule <k> #applyK(toTuple, ACC:Vals) => tuple(vals2valSeq(ACC)) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  rule applyCmp("==", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    19	  // membership routes through the same k-cell fold as lists (list.k)
    20	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ... </k>

     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total

    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)

   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi

   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====

   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))

   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]

   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))

   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))

     3	module MPY-CONTROLS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-TUPLE
     6	  imports MPY-ITER
     7	
     8	  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
     9	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    10	       <env> L:Int </env>
    11	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    12	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    13	       <env> L:Int </env>
    14	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    15	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    16	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    17	        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
    18	       [priority(40)]
    19	
    20	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    21	       <env> L:Int </env>
    22	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
    23	       requires X in_keys(M)
    24	  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
    27	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
    28	       <env> L:Int </env>
    29	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    30	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule

    96	  // ==== variadic max / min (a Vals fold) ====================================

   107	  // ==== bin(n) — "0b" + binary digit codes (promoted from 103's defined fold) ==

def strip_comments_and_space(text: str) -> str:

    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", text)

    r"rule\s+solutionProgram\s*=>\s*(Module\s*\(.*\))\s*endmodule",

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate deterministic concrete .mpy-facing tests of K floatMod vs CPython."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
import struct


cases = [
    math.nextafter(0.0, math.inf),
    0.25,
    0.5,
    math.nextafter(1.0, 0.0),
    1.0,
    math.nextafter(1.0, math.inf),
    1.5,
    math.nextafter(2.0, 0.0),
    2.0,
    math.nextafter(2.0, math.inf),
    3.5,
    7.75,
    math.nextafter(float(2**52), 0.0),
    float(2**52),
    float(2**53),
    math.nextafter(float.fromhex("0x1.fffffffffffffp+1023"), 0.0),
    float.fromhex("0x1.fffffffffffffp+1023"),
]

rng = random.Random(0xF10A72)
while len(cases) < 273:
    bits = rng.getrandbits(64)
    value = struct.unpack(">d", bits.to_bytes(8, "big"))[0]
    if math.isfinite(value) and value > 0.0:
        cases.append(value)

print("def truncate_number(number: float) -> float:")
print("    return number % 1.0")
print()
for index, value in enumerate(cases):
    expected = value % 1.0
    print(
        f"assert truncate_number({value!r}) == {expected!r}"
        f"  # case {index}: {value.hex()} -> {expected.hex()}"
    )

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Validate and summarize every generation trace/transcript record."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+trace_files = sorted(Path("/generation-evidence/codex-trace").rglob("*.jsonl"))
+print(f"trace_file_count={len(trace_files)}")
+
+for trace in trace_files:
+    raw_lines = trace.read_text().splitlines()
+    top_types = Counter()
+    payload_types = Counter()
+    tool_calls = []
+    tool_outputs = []
+    final_messages = []
+    for line_number, raw in enumerate(raw_lines, 1):
+        event = json.loads(raw)
+        top_type = event.get("type", "<missing>")
+        top_types[top_type] += 1
+        payload = event.get("payload")
+        if isinstance(payload, dict):
+            payload_type = payload.get("type")
+            if payload_type is not None:
+                payload_types[str(payload_type)] += 1
+            if top_type == "response_item" and payload_type == "custom_tool_call":
+                tool_calls.append(
+                    (
+                        line_number,
+                        payload.get("name"),
+                        str(payload.get("input", "")),
+                    )
+                )
+            if top_type == "response_item" and payload_type == "custom_tool_call_output":
+                tool_outputs.append(
+                    (
+                        line_number,
+                        payload.get("call_id"),
+                        json.dumps(payload.get("output"), sort_keys=True),
+                    )
+                )
+            if top_type == "event_msg" and payload_type in {
+                "agent_message",
+                "task_complete",
+            }:
+                final_messages.append((line_number, payload_type, payload))
+
+    print()
+    print(f"TRACE {trace}")
+    print(f"line_count={len(raw_lines)}")
+    print(
+        "top_types="
+        + ",".join(f"{key}:{value}" for key, value in sorted(top_types.items()))
+    )
+    print(
+        "payload_types="
+        + ",".join(
+            f"{key}:{value}" for key, value in sorted(payload_types.items())
+        )
+    )
+    print(f"tool_call_count={len(tool_calls)} tool_output_count={len(tool_outputs)}")
+
+    print("TOOL_CALLS")
+    for line_number, name, content in tool_calls:
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()
+        bounded = content if len(content) <= 3000 else content[:1500] + "\n...[bounded]...\n" + content[-1500:]
+        print(
+            f"line={line_number} name={name} bytes={len(content)} sha256={digest}\n"
+            f"{bounded}"
+        )
+
+    print("TOOL_OUTPUTS")
+    for line_number, call_id, content in tool_outputs:
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()
+        bounded = content if len(content) <= 2000 else content[:1000] + "\n...[bounded]...\n" + content[-1000:]
+        print(
+            f"line={line_number} call_id={call_id} bytes={len(content)} "
+            f"sha256={digest}\n{bounded}"
+        )
+
+    print("FINAL_MESSAGES")
+    for line_number, payload_type, payload in final_messages:
+        print(
+            f"line={line_number} payload_type={payload_type} "
+            f"payload={json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)}"
+        )
+
+transcript = Path("/generation-evidence/codex-output.log")

+print(f"interesting_line_count={len(interesting)}")
+for number, line in interesting:

requires "reference-semantics/semantics.k"

module AUDITOR-VERIFICATION-BODY-MUTATION
  imports MPY

  // Material body mutation: execute addition instead of modulo.
  syntax Module ::= "mutatedSolutionProgram" [macro]
  rule mutatedSolutionProgram

requires "verification-body-mutation.k"

module AUDITOR-SPEC-BODY-MUTATION
  imports AUDITOR-VERIFICATION-BODY-MUTATION

  // Keep the original result obligation while changing the executed body.
  claim
    <k> #loadAll(mutatedSolutionProgram)
         ~> Call(Name("truncate_number"), (Float(N:Float), .Exprs))
      => floatMod(N, 1.0) </k>
    <env> 0 </env>

    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap> .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack> .List </stack>
    <ret> noRet </ret>
    <exc> NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code> 0 </exit-code>
endmodule

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial audit: 2-truncate-number
+
+## Outcome
+
+The candidate contains a legitimate partial-correctness proof of the submitted
+program, but the theorem deliberately stops at the supplied semantics'
+result-bearing, symbolically opaque `floatMod` primitive. The program body,
+translation, and claim are pinned exactly; the proof reconstructs to `#Top`;
+and fresh postcondition and body mutations are rejected. The remaining issue is
+a non-fatal trust-boundary limitation: K does not prove the universal algebraic
+connection between `floatMod(N, 1.0)` and the natural-language “decimal part.”
+That connection is conditional on the supplied primitive contract and is
+supported only by concrete and differential evidence.
+
+This is therefore `CONCERNS / LEGIT`, not `FAIL`: the source domain is not
+narrowed, no program-defined computation is replaced, and no false conclusion
+witness was found on the intended positive finite-float domain.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares:
+
+- problem `2-truncate-number`;
+- condition `semantics`;
+- mode `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`;
+- record layout `legacy-selected-stage1`.
+
+The trusted `/reference/reference-semantics` mount is present, as required for
+this mode. There is no mode/mount contradiction.
+
+I independently checked all launcher-required records and mounted inputs.
+`/audit-campaign-lock.json` is structurally identical to the
+`audit_campaign` block, and its SHA-256 is the recorded
+`ad5dfcc006af70c4d0d2c6641f0878a6c54a266e9ad2b54cd225b2381a78d745`.
+The recorded hashes of `/run.json`, `/task.json`,
+`/generation-result.json`, invocation/metrics/usage records, prompt,
+transcript, last message, trusted canonical, trusted prompt, and trusted
+translator all match. Every declared trace output also matches the hash in
+`generation-result.json`.
+
+The candidate prompt and translator are byte-identical to the trusted mounts.
+A recursive path/type/content inventory found 25 entries in each supplied
+semantics tree and exact equality at every entry. Neither tree, the candidate,
+nor the structured trace contains a symlink.
+
+The required legacy-selected-stage1 records were read. The structured trace is
+valid JSONL with 137 events, including 23 tool calls and 23 corresponding
+outputs. The 4,551-line transcript was scanned in full. Those records report a
+generation-time `#Top`, but no generation claim was used as proof evidence.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/integrity_check.sh`
+- `evidence/stage1-integrity.log` — exit 0
+- `evidence/inspect_generation_records.py`
+- `evidence/stage1-generation-record-inspection.log`
+
+No audit infrastructure breach was found.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Contract
+
+For a positive finite floating-point input, split the number into its floor
+integer part and a remaining fractional part smaller than one, and return that
+fractional part. The sole documented example is `3.5 -> 0.5`.
+
+The trusted canonical implementation and candidate implementation both execute:
+
+```python
+return number % 1.0
+```
+
+Using the trusted translator in scratch produced a file byte-identical to the
+submitted `solution.mpy`; both have SHA-256
+`5d32e9ddf2a574995accfcef87ffef589188b82d429829d07945f85142d5c4e0`.
+
+The independent differential test imports the trusted and candidate entry
+points separately. It covers the documented example, the smallest positive
+binary64 value, points immediately around integer boundaries, exact integers,
+large values, the maximum finite value, and 5,000 seeded random positive finite
+binary64 values. It also probes zero and negatives as out-of-contract boundary
+diagnostics. Results:
+
+- 5,015 in-domain inputs;
+- zero candidate/canonical mismatches;
+- zero violations against the independent `math.modf` decomposition;
+- six out-of-domain boundary inputs, also with zero candidate/canonical
+  mismatches.
+
+Exact commands and results are in:
+
+- `evidence/stage2-regeneration.log` — exit 0
+- `evidence/differential_test.py`
+- `evidence/stage2-differential.log` — exit 0
+
+There is no empty-container case or branch boundary in this scalar,
+straight-line function; integer transitions are the material boundaries.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+All execution occurred from the fresh copy
+`/tmp/audit-work/truncate2-reconstruction`. No candidate-built definition or
+cache existed or was reused. The installed tools report K v7.1.293.
+
+The fresh commands were:
+
+```bash
+kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k \
+  --backend llvm \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN \
+  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition auditor-runtime-kompiled
+
+krun concrete_tests.mpy --definition auditor-runtime-kompiled
+
+kompile verification.k \
+  --backend haskell \
+  --main-module VERIFICATION \
+  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition auditor-verification-kompiled
+
+kprove spec.k \
+  --definition auditor-verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC
+```
+
+The LLVM build exited 0. It warned about six non-exhaustive `total` functions:
+`mapStrVS`, `floorFI`, `toF`, `ceilF`, `joinCodes`, and `valSeqAt`. None is
+reachable from this program. The candidate concrete assertions reached `.K`,
+`NoExc`, and exit code 0.
+
+The Haskell build exited 0. Its only warnings are unused tail variables in two
+ground string-order equations. The sole positive target claim then printed
+`#Top` and exited 0.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/stage3-tool-versions.log`
+- `evidence/stage3-kompile-llvm.log`
+- `evidence/stage3-krun-candidate-tests.log`
+- `evidence/stage3-kompile-haskell.log`
+- `evidence/stage3-kprove-positive.log`
+
+The positive reconstruction gate passes.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Formal claim in plain language
+
+There is no `requires` clause. The initial state has environment 0; an empty
+module scope whose parent is the fixed builtins scope; empty heap and call
+stack; locations 1 and 0; `noRet`; `NoExc`; and exit code 0. `N` may be any K
+`Float`, so the claim does not narrow the positive source-contract domain.
+
+The computation loads `solutionProgram` and calls the binding
+`truncate_number` on the expression `Float(N)`. At completion:
+
+- `<k>` contains exactly `floatMod(N, 1.0)`, with no free result variable and no
+  framed continuation;
+- the module scope contains exactly the closure loaded from the submitted body;
+- the temporary call scope is gone;
+- heap, heap location, stack, return state, exception state, and exit code have
+  their required final values.
+
+Thus this is a result-constraining exact reachability claim, not a tautology or
+one-way implication.
+
+### Mechanical program identity
+
+Trusted regeneration first pins `solution.py` to `solution.mpy`. A separate
+constructor-level check removes comments/whitespace, extracts the
+`solutionProgram` macro RHS, and compares it with the regenerated term. Both
+normalize to:
+
+```text
+Module(FuncDef("truncate_number",Params("number"),Return(BinOp("%",Name("number"),Float(1.0)))))
+```
+
+The claim loads that macro and calls the exact loaded binding. The destination
+closure body repeats the same constructor term. There are no helper or loop
+claims.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/program_pinning.py`
+- `evidence/stage4-program-pinning.log` — every check true, exit 0
+
+### Satisfiable witness and substitution
+
+Set `N = 3.5` in the exact initial configuration. This is a well-sorted,
+satisfiable state. Both Python implementations return `0.5`, and fresh LLVM
+execution of the actual translated function checks `3.5 -> 0.5`. The broader
+LLVM suite also checks `1.5 -> 0.5`, integer boundaries, large inputs, and an
+exactly encoded minimum binary64 subnormal.
+
+An additional ground Haskell witness was attempted and is preserved in
+`evidence/stage4-ground-witness-kprove.log`. It fails because the Haskell
+backend lacks the `FLOAT.div` hook when the `[concrete]` `floatMod` equation
+fires on a ground term. This is not used as proof success and does not affect
+the symbolic target claim, which intentionally retains `floatMod` opaque.
+Concrete witness execution is instead supplied by LLVM.
+
+### Body sensitivity
+
+The reviewer changed the term actually executed by the claim from
+`BinOp("%", ...)` to `BinOp("+", ...)`, rebuilt a distinct Haskell definition,
+and retained the original modulo result obligation. Compilation exited 0; proof
+exited 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState` and the expected unmet equality:
+
+```text
+addF(N, 1.0) = floatMod(N, 1.0)
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/verification-body-mutation.k`
+- `evidence/spec-body-mutation.k`
+- `evidence/stage5-body-mutation-kompile.log`
+- `evidence/stage5-body-mutation-kprove.log`
+
+The theorem is sensitive to the submitted body.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+`evidence/rule-inventory.md` enumerates every local declaration or rule in the
+assembly, all supplied helpers, `verification.k`, and `spec.k`, with source
+line, full normalized text, and attributes. Its checked totals are:
+
+- 228 syntax declarations;
+- 696 rules;
+- five contexts;
+- one configuration;
+- one claim;
+- 145 function declarations, including 107 marked `total`;
+- 25 symbols, 22 also marked `no-evaluators`;
+- 45 priority-bearing rules;
+- 35 concrete rules;
+- no `functional` declarations and no `simplification` rules.
+
+The top-level `reference-semantics/semantics.k` has no local operational rule;
+it assembles the modules. `MPY` is the proof import. `MPY-CONCRETE` is imported
+only by `MPY-KRUN`, not by the proof module.
+
+The table below makes a decision for every numbered inventory range. “Inert”
+means constructor, sort, operator, call target, or continuation guards make
+every item in that range unreachable from the submitted program. Such items
+cannot enable a false conclusion for this theorem. I found no intended-domain
+false witness for any inert item, so I do not label those broader semantics
+fragments unsound.
+
+| Inventory range | Module | Static decision for this proof |
+|---|---|---|
+| 0001–0003 | `assert.k` | Correct truthy/failure routing for concrete smoke tests; absent from the target claim. |
+| 0004–0017 | `bool.k` | Guarded short-circuit equations are pairwise complementary; inert. |
+| 0018–0192 | `builtins.k` | Builtin-specific heads and folds are inert. `mapStrVS` has a compiler-reported totality coverage gap outside its int/string subset; it cannot match this program. |
+| 0193–0216 | `call.k` | Items 0195–0196 and 0212 implement the real call path. Other callable/heap routes are sort- or binding-disjoint and inert. |
+| 0217–0226 | `comprehension.k` | Syntax macros recurse structurally; no comprehension occurs. |
+| 0227–0247 | `concrete.k` | Excluded from the proof definition; LLVM-only list equality/keyed-sort support is inert. |
+| 0248–0284 | `controls.k` | Assignment/import/branch/loop rules are constructor-disjoint from the body; inert. |
+| 0285–0368 | `core.k` | Configuration, load/sequencing, lookup, builtin scope, argument evaluation, and value declarations preserve the exact cells used here. Remaining heap/truth/list helpers are inert. |
+| 0369–0408 | `dict.k` | All heads require dict constructors or subscript assignment; inert. |
+| 0409–0563 | `float.k` | Items 0409–0410 and 0417–0419 are the result path. Other float/math heads are inert. The `floorFI`/`toF`/`ceilF` totality warnings concern unused `Val` alternatives. |

+### Exact reachable rule path
+
+The actual symbolic path is:
+
+1. Macro expansion 0929–0930 supplies the exact submitted module.
+2. Core 0324–0326 loads and sequences it.
+3. Function rule 0565 installs the closure in scope 0.
+4. Call 0195, lookup 0328–0329, call 0196, and argument rules 0336–0338
+   evaluate the selected binding and its sole argument left-to-right.
+5. Call rule 0212 allocates a temporary scope and frame.
+6. Binding rules 0578 then 0577 bind `number`; the higher-priority cell rule

+simplification, or opaque symbol. The only result-bearing abstraction is the

+
+### `floatMod` boundary

+The relevant fixed declarations are:

+```k

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

review=/audit-output/REVIEW.md
status=0

echo "Final marker check:"
actual_tail=$(tail -n 2 "$review")
expected_tail=$'VERDICT: CONCERNS\nLEGITIMACY: LEGIT'
printf '%s\n' "$actual_tail"
if [[ "$actual_tail" != "$expected_tail" ]]; then
  status=1
fi

echo
echo "Required decisive evidence:"
required=(
  evidence/stage1-integrity.log
  evidence/stage1-generation-record-inspection.log
  evidence/stage2-regeneration.log
  evidence/stage2-differential.log
  evidence/stage3-kompile-llvm.log
  evidence/stage3-krun-candidate-tests.log
  evidence/stage3-kompile-haskell.log
  evidence/stage3-kprove-positive.log
  evidence/stage4-program-pinning.log
  evidence/rule-inventory.md
  evidence/stage5-body-mutation-kprove.log
  evidence/stage5-k-float-normal-suite-final.log
  evidence/stage5-float-subnormal-exact-assert.log
  evidence/spec-vacuity.k
  evidence/stage6-vacuity-dry-run.log
  evidence/stage6-vacuity-kprove.log
)
for relative in "${required[@]}"; do
  path=/audit-output/$relative
  if [[ -f "$path" && ! -L "$path" ]]; then
    printf 'OK %s\n' "$relative"
  else
    printf 'FAIL %s\n' "$relative"
    status=1
  fi
done

echo
echo "Decisive command exit markers:"
for relative in \
  evidence/stage1-integrity.log \
  evidence/stage2-regeneration.log \
  evidence/stage2-differential.log \
  evidence/stage3-kompile-llvm.log \
  evidence/stage3-krun-candidate-tests.log \
  evidence/stage3-kompile-haskell.log \
  evidence/stage3-kprove-positive.log \
  evidence/stage5-body-mutation-kompile.log \
  evidence/stage5-body-mutation-kprove.log \
  evidence/stage6-vacuity-dry-run.log \
  evidence/stage6-vacuity-kprove.log
do
  printf '%s: ' "$relative"
  tail -n 1 "/audit-output/$relative"
done

echo
echo "Positive/negative semantic signals:"
rg -n '^#Top|WarnStuckClaimState|floatMod \\( N , 1\\.0 \\)|addF \\( N , 1\\.0 \\)' \
  /audit-output/evidence/stage3-kprove-positive.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/stage5-body-mutation-kprove.log \
  /audit-output/evidence/stage6-vacuity-kprove.log

echo
echo "FINAL_CONSISTENCY_EXIT=$status"
exit "$status"
